name: Red 40
description: A synthetic red dye used in candies, cereals, and drinks. Linked to hyperactivity and allergic reactions in sensitive individuals. Some studies suggest possible carcinogenic effects.

name: Yellow 5
description: Also called tartrazine, this dye is used in chips, snacks, and sodas. May trigger hyperactivity and allergic reactions in those sensitive to aspirin or benzoates.

name: Yellow 6
description: Also known as sunset yellow, used in candies, baked goods, and beverages. Linked in animal studies to adrenal and kidney problems.

name: Blue 1
description: Bright blue coloring found in drinks, candy, and desserts. Some evidence suggests potential allergic and neurological effects.

name: Blue 2
description: Indigo carmine dye used in sweets and snacks. Linked in animal studies to possible brain tumors at high exposure levels.

name: Green 3
description: Synthetic green dye used in mint candies and snacks. Associated with bladder and thyroid effects in animal tests.

name: Red 3
description: Erythrosine dye used in cherries and icings. Shown to cause thyroid tumors in animals and banned from cosmetics.

name: Aspartame
description: Low-calorie sweetener found in diet snacks and drinks. Must be avoided by those with PKU. Linked to headaches and mood changes in sensitive individuals.

name: Sucralose
description: Artificial sweetener sold as Splenda. May disrupt gut bacteria and affect insulin response when consumed often.

name: Saccharin
description: Oldest artificial sweetener used in sugar-free gums and diet foods. Linked to bladder cancer in early studies, though considered safe in small amounts today.

name: Acesulfame K
description: Artificial sweetener often combined with aspartame or sucralose. May impact metabolism and gut bacteria based on some studies.

name: Neotame
description: Powerful artificial sweetener similar to aspartame. Limited long-term data; may affect metabolism in high amounts.

name: Advantame
description: Newer sweetener derived from aspartame. Limited research but some concern about metabolic side effects.

name: Sodium Nitrite
description: Used to preserve meats like bacon and sausages. Can form nitrosamines, carcinogenic compounds when cooked at high heat.

name: Sodium Nitrate
description: Preservative and color stabilizer in cured meats. Linked to increased colorectal cancer risk.

name: Sodium Benzoate
description: Used in sodas and acidic foods. When mixed with vitamin C, can form benzene, a known carcinogen.

name: Potassium Sorbate
description: Mold-preventing preservative in cheeses and baked goods. May cause skin irritation in sensitive people.

name: BHA
description: Butylated hydroxyanisole, a fat preservative found in chips and cereals. Classified as a possible human carcinogen.

name: BHT
description: Butylated hydroxytoluene, used with BHA to prevent rancidity. May disrupt hormones and cause organ effects in animals.

name: Propyl Gallate
description: Used in oils and processed foods to prevent spoilage. May cause allergic reactions and hormone disruption.

name: Sodium Metabisulfite
description: Preservative in dried fruits, wines, and snack seasonings. Can cause asthma or allergic reactions.

name: Calcium Propionate
description: Mold inhibitor in bread and bakery products. Linked to hyperactivity and migraines in some people.

name: Sodium Erythorbate
description: Used with nitrites in meats. High intake can strain kidneys and cause metabolic imbalance.

name: Monosodium Glutamate
description: Flavor enhancer in soups, noodles, and chips. Some report headaches or flushing after high intake.

name: Disodium Inosinate
description: Flavor enhancer often paired with MSG. Can cause mild throat irritation in sensitive individuals.

name: Disodium Guanylate
description: Used with MSG to intensify savory flavors. May cause allergic reactions or sensitivity in some.

name: Hydrolyzed Vegetable Protein
description: Flavor additive containing free glutamates similar to MSG. Can cause headaches or allergic responses in sensitive individuals.

name: Partially Hydrogenated Oil
description: Main source of trans fats in processed foods. Raises bad cholesterol and lowers good cholesterol, contributing to heart disease.

name: Refined Palm Oil
description: Cheap oil used in baked goods and chips. Overheating produces oxidation compounds harmful to heart health.

name: Interesterified Fat
description: Modified fat used as a trans-fat substitute. Can disrupt insulin sensitivity and lipid metabolism.

name: Artificial Flavoring
description: Synthetic chemicals used to mimic natural flavors. Can trigger allergies and digestive irritation in some individuals.

name: High Fructose Corn Syrup
description: Sweetener in sodas and processed snacks. Overconsumption leads to insulin resistance, obesity, and liver fat buildup.

name: Maltodextrin
description: Highly processed carbohydrate filler. Rapidly spikes blood sugar and can disrupt gut health.

name: Titanium Dioxide
description: Whitening agent used in candies and sauces. Classified as possibly carcinogenic and may cause DNA damage in large amounts.

name: Carrageenan
description: Thickener from seaweed used in dairy and vegan foods. Degraded forms can cause gut inflammation.

name: Polysorbate 80
description: Emulsifier in ice cream and sauces. Linked to gut barrier disruption and fertility issues in animal studies.

name: Propylene Glycol
description: Used to retain moisture in snacks. Overexposure can irritate skin and may be toxic in large quantities.

name: Sodium Phosphate
description: Used in processed meats and baked snacks. High intake burdens kidneys and affects calcium levels.

name: Potassium Bromate
description: Dough conditioner used in breads. Classified as a possible human carcinogen; banned in several countries.

name: Aluminum Sulfate
description: Used in baking powders and processed cheese. Excess aluminum exposure can affect brain and bone health.

name: Sodium Aluminum Phosphate
description: Leavening agent in baked products. Contributes to aluminum accumulation when consumed frequently.

name: Sodium Hexametaphosphate
description: Used to prevent discoloration in foods. Long-term consumption can deplete calcium and essential minerals.

name: Azodicarbonamide
description: Flour bleaching and dough-improving agent. Breaks down into potentially harmful compounds and is banned in many countries.

name: Propylene Glycol Alginate
description: Thickener used in salad dressings and desserts. Large doses may affect liver and kidney function.

name: Calcium Disodium Edta
description: Preservative and stabilizer in dressings and canned foods. Excess use may deplete essential minerals like zinc and iron.

name: Sodium Stearoyl Lactylate
description: Emulsifier used in baked goods. May cause digestive irritation when consumed frequently.
